verdict.rationale: Superset lets a developer describe a task (e.g., a bug report) as a prompt, launch a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) that works autonomously in an isolated worktree, and then review/commit/PR the fix via the diff viewer — covering the end-to-end autonomous workflow for a bug fix. However, this relies entirely on the underlying agent's own diagnostic capability; Superset itself provides no bug-specific diagnosis features (e.g., log analysis, reproduction, test verification) beyond generic prompt-driven task launch and orchestration. Missing for 10: evidence of autonomous root-cause diagnosis, test-driven verification of the fix, or a hands-on report of Superset resolving a real reported bug end-to-end.
